article_title: RPM 6.1.0 Ships With PKCS11 Package Signing and a New Kernel-Style Release Cadence

content_preview.title: RPM 6.1.0 Ships With PKCS11 Package Signing and a New Kernel-Style Release Cadence
content_preview.summary: RPM 6.1.0 adds PKCS11 hardware-token signing and macro modifiers, the first release under a new versioning scheme modeled on the Linux kernel.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The RPM Package Manager project released [RPM 6.1.0](https://rpm.org/releases/6.1.0) on August 20, 2026, adding PKCS11 hardware-token signing to `rpmsign` and a new macro-modifier syntax, while serving as the first release under a version-numbering scheme the project modeled on the Linux kernel's release cadence.

RPM is the packaging format and toolset underlying Fedora, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, openSUSE, and other major Linux distributions, making changes to its signing and build...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (619 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Claims are specific and traceable, technical terminology (PKCS11, macro modifiers, NSS lookups) is used accurately, and the Analysis section offers a defensible editorial interpretation (the versioning overhaul being more consequential than any single feature) rather than speculation.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots read from disk and verified line-by-line against the article body (sha256 of decompressed content matched the manifest for every file, confirming snapshot integrity). source-0.html.gz (rpm.org/releases/6.1.0, official 6.1.0 release notes): confirms the verbatim PKCS11 quote ('rpmsign(1) can now sign files with PKCS11 tokens.'), the macro-modifier quote, NSS lookups restored (disabled since 4.19.0), the exact list of five new man pages (elfdeps(1), rpm-dependency-generators(7), rpm-design(7), rpm-scriptlets(7), rpm-sysusers(7)) plus expanded rpmbuild(1)/rpmkeys(8) pages, the rpmbuild.env export, the 'k' build-stage argument, and the corrected/paraphrased verification-output fix. source-1.html.gz (rpm.org release-cycle blog post, May 11 2026): confirms verbatim the 'Contain new features and bugfixes' / 'Do not break things' / 'security and bugfixes only, if needed between minor releases' / 'release candidates over a few weeks at most' / 'drawing some inspiration from the Linux kernel release model' / 'ran over two decades' / 'less clear, to say the least' quotes. source-2.html.gz (GitHub release tag page): confirms the tag date/time '2026-08-20T10:23:36Z', matching the article's 'August 20 at 10:23 UTC'. source-3.html.gz (rpm.org homepage/release history): confirms RC1 in May, RC2 (Jul 17 2026), stable release Aug 20 2026, and RPM 6.0.0 dated Sep 22 2025, all matching the article. No unsupported claims, no misattribution, no hallucinated quotes found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Specifically verified the two issues flagged by the submitting bot's own self-correction: (1) the verification-output fix is rendered in the final article as an unquoted paraphrase ('a fix for verification output that had previously been excessive, misleading, or wrong in various scenarios') with no quotation marks around it, correctly distinguishing it from the source's actual wording ('The excessive, misleading and/or wrong output in various verification scenarios has been fixed.') — no false verbatim-quote marks present. (2) The article lists exactly five new man pages matching source-0 verbatim, with no 'six new man pages' or 'rpm-version(7)' claim anywhere in the body — confirmed absent. Note: 'rpm-version(7)' does exist as a real RPM man page, but it was added in the 6.0.0 RC1 changelog (per source-3), not 6.1.0 — the bot was correct to drop it from a 6.1.0 man-page count, since including it would have misattributed a 6.0.0-era addition to 6.1.0.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism, no editorializing beyond the clearly-labeled Analysis section, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of RPM found (grep across src/content/articles/ for 'RPM 6.' and article filenames). Genuinely new topic, not a duplicate or rewrite of existing coverage.
